label: Recycling: the trunk reads its own output
context: Show the trunk as a box 'Pairformer stack' with an input arrow from 'input embeddings s_inputs, z_init'. Next to it a small 8×8 pair matrix z that starts noisy/unstructured (random grey shades) and a tiny predicted 2D chain of 12 beads (the distogram-implied structure) that starts tangled. Each recycling pass (counter 'pass 1 / 4' … '4 / 4'): the output s and z go through a LayerNorm+linear box labelled 'recycle' along a curved arrow back and are ADDED to the next pass's input (draw a ⊕). With each pass the pair matrix becomes more structured (clear dark band near diagonal and two off-diagonal contact blocks) and the chain untangles into a hairpin. Caption phases: 'pass 1: first guess from the inputs', 'passes 2–4: the trunk refines its own output', 'gradients flow only through the last pass in training'. End with 'c = (s, z) handed to the denoiser'. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: Recycling: the trunk reads its own output
spec.caption: Four passes through the Pairformer stack: s and z are normalised, linearly projected and added back to the next pass's input. The pair matrix sharpens and the implied chain untangles into a hairpin before c = (s, z) goes to the denoiser.
